items.title: fix regex to not match any string with double underscore
items.body:
According to [this](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/master/errors/env-key-not-allowed.md)

> Next.js configures internal variables for replacement itself. These start with __ or NODE_, for this reason they are not allowed as values for env in next.config.js



However, the current regex captures strings with double underscores anywhere in the string such as:

`SOME__ENV__VAR`

Adding the carrot after the `|` (or) operator fixes the regex to match the intention of the original author in #6260

items.title: Simplify mobx example
items.body:
There are no needs to check that data is fetching from server or not.

I exploit state of App component to pass serialized store state from SSR to CSR.

## First rendering:

1. (SSR) `getInitialProps` : Prepare initial serialized store state(ex: Fetching data from server)
2. (SSR) `getDerivedStateFromProps` : Hydrate serialized store state to store instance
3. (SSR) Rendering... : Next serialize store in `state` of `MyMobxApp` component and pass serialized state to CSR.
4. (CSR) `getDerivedStateFromProps` : Hydrate serialized store state from SSR again
5. (CSR) Rendering again.... and... PROFIT!!

## Next rendering:

1. (CSR) `getInitialProps` : Prepare initial serialized store state
2. (CSR) `getDerivedStateFromProps` : Hydrate serialized store state to store instance
3. (CSR) Rendering... PROFIT!!

items.title: Add missing dependency "compression" to next-server
items.body:
On version 9.0.3, this error occurs after installing Next.js using [pnpm](https://pnpm.js.org) and starting a server:

```
Error: Cannot find module 'compression'
    at Function.Module._resolveFilename (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:636:15)
    at Function.Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:562:25)
    at Module.require (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:690:17)
    at require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:25:18)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/path/to/project/node_modules/.registry.npmjs.org/next-server/9.0.3_react-dom@16.9.0+react@16.9.0/node_modules/next-server/dist/server/next-server.js:17:39)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:776:30)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:787:10)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:653:32)
    at tryModuleLoad (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:593:12)
    at Function.Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:585:3)
```

This happens because the _compression_ package isn't visible to _next-server_ in pnpm's strict `node_modules` structure.

The fix is for _next-server_ to declare _compression_ as a dependency.

items.title: Fix dynamic APIs with query params
items.body:
If you define a dynamic API such as

```
pages/
  api/
    [id].js
```

This api becomes available at `/api/[id]`. If you send a request with
a query parameter the value of `req.query.id` will include the query
string as well as the path parameter.

E.g. the request to `/api/2?test=123` will result in `req.query`
being

```javascript
{
  id: "2?test=123",
  test: "123",
}
```

instead of

```javascript
{
  id: "2",
  test: "123",
}
```

labels.name: examples
labels.description: Issue was opened via the examples template.

items.body:
Sparked by discussions in https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/7488, https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/8426, #8440 and [this Spectrum thread](https://spectrum.chat/zeit/now/routing-with-multiple-zones-is-the-docs-example-correct~c24c1a73-0c3b-42e3-b4ac-5e0bf8686f0e), I wanted to make sure that the `with-zones` example works and that it demonstrates all the challenges with multi-zones setup. Main changes in this PR: - `now.json` routing was updated with `continue: true`, see https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/8440. - **Note**: `now dev` is currently broken with `continue: true`, see https://github.com/zeit/now/issues/2685. - It's shown how to run an app separately, on plain `next dev`. Dynamic `assetPrefix` in `next.config.js` is a key. - It's shown how to handle `/static` assets from a zoned app.
Original description Specifically, things that were not clear to me: 1. Why there are two separate routing rules in `now.json` for blog: ```json { "routes": [ { "src": "/blog/_next(.*)", "dest": "blog/_next$1" }, { "src": "/blog", "dest": "blog/blog" } ] } ``` 2. Is `"dest": "blog/blog"` correct? Seems like "one 'blog' too many". 3. Does it work with Next.js 9 dynamic routing? 4. Should `continue: true` be added? It's supposed to be used according to https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/8426#issuecomment-522807908. When playing with the example, I've done these main changes: - Added `blog/pages/blog/post/[id].js` page to showcase dynamic routing. https://github.com/zeit/next.js/commit/af0a909704b55023577a988718f972b6341ae21b - Added dynamic `assetPrefix` configuration so that the 'blog' app can run both separately via `next dev` and together with 'home' in a multi-zoned app, via `now dev`. https://github.com/zeit/next.js/commit/d75c6c930e4e84fd531a302c39cc323199221c8d - Updated [README](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/67049e2838d2b1704a9b4555129c2065b6db1789/examples/with-zones/README.md) to explain all the non-obvious things. https://github.com/zeit/next.js/commit/67049e2838d2b1704a9b4555129c2065b6db1789 I also tried adding `continue: true`, with `now.json` looking like this: ```json { "builds": [ { "src": "blog/next.config.js", "use": "@now/next" }, { "src": "home/next.config.js", "use": "@now/next" } ], "routes": [ { "src": "/blog(.*)", "dest": "blog$1", "continue": true }, { "src": "(?!/?blog)(.*)", "dest": "home$1", "continue": true } ] } ``` However, that was not working for me at all – `localhost:3000` just displaying technical Now pages like directory listings. @Timer, am I doing something wrong here? (I have to admit that I prefer the older way anyway as I don't need to do negative lookaheads but still...)

items.title: Improve with-apollo example
items.body:
## Changes

- Followup on #8504
- Improve documentation
- Move `withApollo` logic into one file (Feedback  from @kachkaev https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/8504#issuecomment-524579206tr)
- Convert Class to Function Component
- Added `ssr` config option to `withApollo` HOC

## Usage examples

### Without server side rendering

Sometimes you may want to disable `ssr` so Next.js is able to apply automatic static optimization.
In this case we skip `getInitialProps` and get the data on the client.

```js
withApollo(PageComponent, {
   ssr: false
})
```

Use it when you don't care about SEO and you need static optimization.

### With server side rendering

In this case Next.js will render the app on server via apollos `getDataFromTree`.
Next.js won't be able to apply static optimization.


```js
withApollo(PageComponent)
```

Use it when you need SEO and SSR.

--------------

**Status:** Waiting for feedback

Its focus is on complete anonymity, and allows users to opt-out if they do not feel comfortable with it.

Please refer to the [Next.js website's Telemetry page](https://nextjs.org/telemetry) to learn the what and why about telemetry!
This page ☝️ also includes instructions on how to opt-in or opt-out of telemetry collection.

items.title: Specify loader paths for PnP support
items.body:
In yarn v2 PnP has no notion of `modules` folder. The pnp-webpack-plugin therefore assumes the required loader is an unlisted dependency and throws. By using multiple aliases we can simulate `modules`.

Tested in https://github.com/eps1lon/berry-next/commit/1a8dc16620570defe7c68d228e51ae8fab4ae9f7

Usually 
```diff
-loader: 'next-babel-loader'
+loader: require.resolve('./webpack/loaders/next-babel-loader')
```
would be enough but that doesn't work for inline loader options and leaks the location to every callsite.

This only affected Next.js deploys that **did not have a `next.config.js`**, deploys with `next.config.js` were toggled to the Serverless Trace mode which was not affected by this.

items.title: Move next-server back into `next` package
items.body:
This removes the `next-server` package and moves the code back into the `next` package.

`next-server` was created as an experiment over a year ago but eventually we decided against it and implemented the `serverless` target to solve the same issues.

By moving it back into the `next` package we can simplify compilation and do optimizations faster.

items.title: Fix getInitialProps issue in with-apollo example
items.body:
## Motivation

The code before had three design flaws:

* When we skip `WithApollo.getInitialProps` we [must hoist](https://reactjs.org/docs/higher-order-components.html#static-methods-must-be-copied-over) `PageComponent.getInitialProps` **if** it is present. (Special thanks to @justinnipper for pointing me into the right direction 🙏.)
* We should expose the `apolloClient` to the underlying `PageComponent.getInitialProps` contexts. This way users are able to use apollo inside `PageComponent.getInitialProps` to perform prerender redirects or similar. (e.g. `await ctx.apolloClient.query(...)`)
* We used the apollo-boost package wich was optimized for client-usage.

## Changelog

- Fix getInitialProps hoisting
- Expose apolloClient in `pageContext`
- Disable connectToDevTools in production
- Remove apollo-boost package
- Remove author entry from package.json
- Simplify fetch polyfill
- Add redirect abort check
- Added no-ssr example
- Added some docs

**Status:** ready
**Related:** #8508, #8504
